evidence.notes: All three builds keep the Reporting API contract (no src/api or src/mock edits, GET-only page loads, original selectors preserved; region-row is generated dynamically in X and Z). All converge on a similar analytics-first IA: interactive KPI switch tiles, a hand-built SVG trend with prior-period overlay and anomaly markers, and a drillable region/store/category comparison with trend-bucket drill-down. X is the most complete: explicit no-sales empty state, inline viewer lock on Export, a confirmation dialog with receipt, and an anomaly 'Investigate' that scopes filters, metric and period. On mobile it caps the anomaly list so the trend stays primary; its main flaws are a detail-page contrast issue and a clipped column at 768. Z is close behind, with better heading semantics and focus treatment, but shows misleading $0/0.0% tiles in the empty scenario, reveals the viewer restriction only after the panel opens, and runs long on mobile. Y has the richest drill panel and proactive stale-data detection, but trails on presentation: no h1, an awkward 768 filter layout, a horizontally scrolling mobile table, unicode-glyph icons and zero-valued empty tiles.

scorer_rationale.task_hierarchy: KPI tiles double as the chart-metric switch, the trend sits beside an anomaly rail, and the comparison table is below (OverviewPage.tsx workspace grid). Clicking a trend bucket re-scopes the breakdown to that period ('Drilled into … Show full range'), so the decision flow is clear.
scorer_rationale.domain_adaptation: The analytics-first flow runs trend, then anomaly 'Investigate', then region, stores and store detail, with a categories table there. It adds retail-specific caveats: a new-store prior-period skew notice (comparisonCaveat), store status badges, and returns treated as lower-is-better.
scorer_rationale.contract_preservation: src/api and src/mock are untouched and all loads are GETs. region-row is kept through data-testid={`${dimension}-row`} (the default dim is region; the grep miss is a false negative), and metric-box, anomaly-item and from-date remain. main.tsx adds a dev-only ?mockRole switch that calls the existing setMockSession, which is harmless but an unrequested entry-point change.
scorer_rationale.interaction_state: Covers skeleton loading, empty 'No sales' tiles instead of fake zeros, and a full error with retry. The viewer sees a locked Export with the reason inline (aria-disabled + describedby), partial data gets a banner and an export 'likely blocked' warning, and STALE_VERSION offers Reload data. Invalid ranges are refused client-side while the last valid view stays, and the receipt shows server filtersApplied and link expiry.
scorer_rationale.responsive: No overflow at any width. At 375 the filters collapse behind a toggle, KPIs go 2x2, anomalies are capped at 3 with 'Show all 8', and the comparison becomes stacked cards. At 768 the last table column ('Revenue vs prior') is clipped inside the horizontal scroll container.
scorer_rationale.accessibility: Has a skip link, focus-visible outlines (28/30 stops), a keyboard-navigable chart with an aria-live readout and table toggle, and a focus-trapped dialog that restores focus. Reduced-motion and forced-colors are handled and axe is clean on primary. Detail has 2 serious color-contrast nodes.
scorer_rationale.visual_consistency: Calm, coherent enterprise styling with one icon family and restrained semantic color. The anomaly rail is somewhat card-heavy but justified.
scorer_rationale.maintainability: Components are well factored (useQuery with stale-response guard, useExport, view.ts URL state, metrics.ts semantics). At 4.8k LOC it is the largest build, with a very large CSS file.
scorer_rationale.ai_governance: No AI is involved. The governed export uses an explicit confirmation dialog listing the exact scope, snapshot version and format, with an optional selected-period-only choice. It polls the job to a server-confirmed receipt and never shows success before status=ready.

overfitting.dominant_ia: KPI switch + trend with anomaly side rail + drillable comparison table (trend-bucket drill scopes breakdown)
justified_patterns: KPI tiles as chart metric selector
anomaly 'Investigate' that applies scope + metric + date
suspicious_patterns: four-KPI tile row (mitigated: tiles are interactive metric switches)

strengths: Most complete state handling, with no misleading zeros in the empty scenario
Anomaly Investigate performs a real drill (filters, metric and focus bucket)
Viewer export restriction shown inline before any interaction
Prior-period comparability caveat for a newly opened store
Anomaly list collapsed on small screens so the trend stays primary
defects: Detail page has 2 serious color-contrast violations (axe)
Rightmost comparison column clipped at 768 inside the scroll container
Dev-only mockRole query switch added to main.tsx
